transcript.text: Zanussi dishwasher keeps tripping the electrics, not every time though. Usually about 15 mins in. Model ZDT21006FA

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. Do not use the dishwasher again until it has been checked by a qualified appliance engineer. A trip around 15 minutes into a programme most often points to an insulation leak developing as the machine reaches its heating stage, commonly the heater/heating assembly; the circulation pump or its wiring are the next possibilities. If it trips immediately on starting, the mains filter, supply cable or moisture in the base becomes more likely instead. With it switched off and unplugged, you can only safely look for obvious damage to the plug/cable and any water visible beneath or around the machine—do not remove panels or restart it to test. Which device trips at the consumer unit, and does it happen after the wash has started circulating?

candidates: Heater or heating assembly insulation fault (high)
Circulation pump or its wiring leaking to earth (medium)
Mains filter, cable or water in the base (low)

reading.symptom: keeps tripping the electrics, usually about 15 minutes into a cycle

plan: Safety: a supply trip hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Zanussi; model ZDT21006FA.
The fault they reported is: "keeps tripping the electrics, usually about 15 minutes into a cycle". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

asked.text: Which device trips at the consumer unit, and does it happen after the wash has started circulating?
